close_reason: Won't fix — engineering impact is per-bead-description 'small (filter values usually shallow)'; both available fix paths (raw JSON walk OR add serde direct dep) cost more than the savings warrant. See close comment for the cost-benefit analysis.
description:
metadata.rs:560: let filter: Filter<...> = match serde_json::from_value(filter_val.clone()) { ... }. The clone is necessary because args is borrowed immutably and serde_json::from_value consumes its argument. The cost is one Value tree clone per /query and /queryChanges call.

Impact at scale: every /query call pays the cost of cloning a JSON tree just to inspect it for the relatedIds-without-relatedType constraint. The generic handler then re-parses the filter from the original args (which is moved into it), so it's a second from_value over essentially the same data.

This is small (filter values are usually shallow), but compounds across the workspace if the same pattern propagates to other extension-server crates. Solution: walk the JSON value directly without going through serde — write a function that takes &Value and checks for the constraint at JSON level. Tradeoff: less type-safe but no clone.
title: validate_metadata_filter clones the entire filter JSON value (filter_val.clone()) just to feed it to from_value, when from_value(filter_val.clone()) is the entry condition
